Name: Asturhealth
Description:
Distributor of an advanced interactive robot developed by AIST, a pioneering leading Japanese research center for industrial automation. It allows the documented benefits of animal therapy to be applied to patients in settings such as nursing homes, nursing homes, or hospitals, where live animals pose treatment difficulties or logistical complexities.

The scientific literature shows that the PARO – NUKA robot reduces stress for the patient and their caregivers
PARO – NUKA stimulates interaction between patients and caregivers
PARO – NUKA has been shown to have a psychological effect on patients, improving their relaxation and motivation.
PARO – NUKA improves the socialization of patients among themselves and with caregivers
PARO – NUKA is the eighth generation of a design that has been in use in Japan and throughout Europe since 2003. It has thousands of users worldwide.

PARO – NUKA has five types of sensors: tactile, light, hearing, temperature and posture sensors, with which it can perceive people and their surroundings. With the light sensor, the robot can recognize light and dark. It feels, through the tactile sensor, if it is caressed and if it is hit; or what position you are in thanks to the posture sensor. PARO – NUKA can also recognize which direction the voice is coming from, and words like your name, greetings and praise thanks to its audio sensor.

PARO – NUKA can learn to behave in the way the user prefers and respond to its new name. For example, if you hit it every time you touch it, PARO – NUKA will remember your previous action and try to repeat that action to make it hit. If you hit it, the seal robot remembers its previous action and tries not to do that action.

When interacting with people, PARO – NUKA responds as if it were alive, moving its head and legs, making sounds, and displaying its preferred behavior.

PARO – NUKA also imitates the voice of a real baby harp seal, an animal that inspired the Japanese engineer who created the robot.

Name: CompMech Research Group
Description:
COMPMECH research group was created by some members of the Mechanical Engineering Department at University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU). Their purpose was to work together in the field of Mechanisms and Machines Theory, Robotics and Computational Mechanics. 

Nowadays, the group is formed by 16 members and our research focuses mainly on the design and analysis of different variants of parallel manipulators – compliant parallel manipulators, reconfigurable parallel manipulators and mechatronics of parallel manipulators. Parallel manipulators are a special type of industrial robots characterized by their architecture – a fixed platform is joined to a mobile platform by several parallel kinematic chains. Due to their high stiffness, accuracy and speed, they have many applications, such as aeronautical applications, machine tool, haptic devices in tele-surgery, assembly lines automation or orientation of solar panels.

Name: Service and Industrial Robotics Lab -UPC
Description: The research group Service and Industrial Robotics of the Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya - BarcelonaTech performs its research activity in industrial and service robotics following traditional approaches as well as new paradigms where the robots are allowed to work safely alongside humans in such a way that they become collaborative coworkers and fellows in the factory floor and at home. In this scope, the research work of the group is mainly focused on transversal tools for dexterous, mobile and cooperative manipulation as well as for robot teleoperation. The list of addressed topics includes robot kinematics and dynamics, control and communications, relational positioning, vision systems and 3D augmented reality, automatic synthesis of grasps, telemanipulation, programming by demonstration, human-like motion planning, simultaneous task and motion planning, and physics-based manipulation planning. Typical tools used in this research are haptic devices, mobile platforms, industrial robots, dual-arm robots, mechanical hands and sensory systems.

Name: URBANODE
Description:
URBANODE is the open communication protocol for Robot-to-Infrastructure (R2I) interaction. We enable autonomous emitters — delivery robots, humanoid robots, drones, and accessibility devices — to securely communicate with urban infrastructure: traffic signals, building doors, elevators, doorbells, package lockers, and charging stations.
One SDK integration. Every certified node. Every city.
Our protocol provides mutual cryptographic authentication (ECDSA P-256, TLS 1.3), a five-dimensional permission matrix, embedded safety rules where the physical node is always the final authority, real-time infrastructure state monitoring, and automatic usage settlement between operators and infrastructure owners.
URBANODE is pure software — no proprietary hardware. Existing infrastructure gets upgraded via firmware update. We are seeking integration partners: robot operators, infrastructure manufacturers, and smart city platforms.
